chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the one who slanders chaste women, whether his testimony is accepted after the legal penalty if he repents? He said: Yes. I said: And what is his repentance? He said: He comes and belies himself in the presence of the Imam and says: 'I had forged [the charge] against so-and-so,' and he repents from what he said.

key_terms.الْمُحْصَنَاتِ: chaste women (those who are married or free from fornication)
key_terms.يَقْذِفُ: slanders (specifically in legal context of qadhf)

ai.seo_question: What constitutes valid repentance for a slanderer to have his testimony accepted after the hadd penalty?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the slanderer's testimony is reinstated upon repentance, defining repentance not merely as internal remorse but as a public declaration of falsehood before the Imam. This procedural requirement underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on restoring social justice and the victim's honor by formally retracting the specific accusation, thereby distinguishing it from general tawbah.
